Verifying structured output — XML, CSV, JSON — is **data verification**: parse
it, then assert on what it says. The bundled `sample_data/results.xml` is a
junit-style test report. `Get Element Attribute` reads an attribute off an
element; `Get Elements` gathers every match across the document. Verify the
report's headline numbers.

## Task 1 — Verify a junit-style results file

**Goal:** create `checks/results.robot` that parses the report, reads its
`failures` attribute, and counts every test case across the suites.

Here is the same attribute-and-count flow over a small inline report. Adapt it
to the results file.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    XML

*** Test Cases ***
Read A Results Summary
    ${root}=    Parse XML    <testsuite failures="2"><testcase/><testcase/><testcase/></testsuite>
    ${failures}=    Get Element Attribute    ${root}    failures
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${failures}    2
    ${cases}=    Get Elements    ${root}    testcase
    Length Should Be    ${cases}    3
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** the suite defines `Test Results Show One Failure`.

<!-- hint -->
Parse the file with `${root}=    Parse XML    sample_data/results.xml`, then read
its failure count with `Get Element Attribute    ${root}    failures` — it is `1`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
The cases live one level down, so use a nested path:
`Get Elements    ${root}    testsuite/testcase`, then
`Length Should Be    ${cases}    6`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    XML

*** Test Cases ***
Test Results Show One Failure
    ${root}=    Parse XML    sample_data/results.xml
    ${failures}=    Get Element Attribute    ${root}    failures
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${failures}    1
    ${cases}=    Get Elements    ${root}    testsuite/testcase
    Length Should Be    ${cases}    6
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run it green

Run:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

**Check:** the report shows one failure across six test cases — Part 5 complete.
